newsitem.title: USA: SIS says to acquire Glastonbury Bank.
newsitem.headline: SIS says to acquire Glastonbury Bank.

text.p: SIS Bancorp Inc said on Monday that it had signed a definitive agreement to acquire all of the outstanding shares of Glastonbury Bank & Trust Co in a deal valued at roughly $40.6 million.
The transaction will take the form of a tax-free exchange of 0.74 share of SIS common stock for each of Glastonbury's 1,829,920 shares of common stock, the holding company said in a statement.
Based on the per share closing price for SIS common stock on August 15, 1997, Glastonbury shareholders would receive $22.20 in SIS common stock for each share of Glastonbury common stock.

"SIS expects to take a pre-tax charge of $2.5 million in 1997 to cover merger related expenses, and expects the merger to have a positive impact on earnings per share in 1998 and beyond," SIS projected.
In connection with the merger, SIS directors have rescinded their existing authorization for SIS to repurchase up to 286,180 shares of SIS common stock, it added.
SIS said the transaction would be recorded as a pooling of interests and is subject to approval by both companies' shareholders.
Under the agreement, Glastonbury, a Connecticut commercial bank with $261.3 million in assets, would become a wholly owned subsidiary of SIS, the company said.
